name: Vancomycin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 15–20 mg/kg (actual body weight) IV every 8–12 hours, AUC-guided (target 400–600 mg·h/L); loading 20–35 mg/kg (maximum 3 g) if critically ill (Rybak 2020). Label alternative: 2 g/day (500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours), infused over at least 60 minutes

key_interactions.effect: More acute kidney injury than vancomycin alone.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Other nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs (concurrent or sequential, systemic or topical)

key_interactions.action: Infuse vancomycin before anesthesia induction as the label advises.

common: Label lists as most common: anaphylaxis, vancomycin infusion reaction, acute kidney injury, hearing loss, neutropenia
serious: Infusion reactions with rapid infusion (hypotension, shock, cardiac arrest)

contraindications: Dextrose-containing solutions: possible contraindication in corn allergy

pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 75% in urine in 24 hours (glomerular filtration)
pk.dialyzability: Yes with high-flux HD: substantial removal each session (median 31% per session high-flux vs 17% low-flux in Petejova 2012); the label's 'poorly removed by dialysis' reflects older low-flux membranes. Hemofiltration and polysulfone hemoperfusion also increase clearance (label).

sources.citation: Baxter Healthcare Corporation. (2026). VANCOMYCIN HYDROCHLORIDE (vancomycin hydrochloride) [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA050671, set ID 99e523d8-9bde-43cb-8434-497015e5dcbd, version effective June 9, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

draft_notes: Selected label is a premixed bag (Baxter, dextrose diluent). 'Infuse before anesthesia induction' paraphrases label 2.1/7.1; confirm wording.
The label's 'poorly removed by dialysis' reflects older membranes; the approved renal text already flags high-flux removal. Decide whether the PK dialyzability line needs the same caveat.
Monitoring frequency (auditory, blood counts) not specified by the label sections read; confirm or simplify.

revision_log.change: PK dialyzability caveat for high-flux HD.
Adult dose: weight-based, AUC-guided with loading; label 2 g/day as alternative.
